boundedSlice.description: Closed frozen plan, command compiler and hermetic lifecycle core for a future one-shot read-only source dump and disposable restore verification.

localClosures: The plan is deep-canonicalized, byte-bound to nine executable inputs and rejects Python bool/int or string-subclass aliasing.

The pg_dump client is pinned to the reviewed linux/amd64 child digest and exact PostgreSQL 17.11 version; the dump command uses Docker stdin, a tmpfs 0600 passfile, no password prompt, no-sync forbidden, bounded resources and the exact attested source container ID.
The source attestation rejects elevated role, database, schema, table-write, sequence-mutation, function-execute, other-schema, RLS and large-object capability gaps.
Source, dump and restore container IDs must be literal 64-hex and pairwise distinct; cleanup for unknown or colliding targets is skipped and marked uncertain.
Never-invoked source, dump and restore stages receive no unbound close or cleanup callbacks.
Caller-owned archive and secret descriptors are protected with duplicates, and partial descriptor-acquisition failures close already acquired descriptors.
Registered files and the workspace retain open inode bindings; post-unlink and post-rmdir device, inode and link-count checks detect rename, replacement and hardlink races.
Cleanup claims are limited to registered workspace paths and exact ID-bound container lifetimes; external copies and physical erasure remain explicitly unproved.
Dump and restore attestations are closed and strictly typed; restore must attest no-owner and no-privileges application.
Cancellation, cleanup uncertainty and a returned-after-deadline lifecycle are terminal and never authorize automatic retry.

The frozen production migration profile is content-addressed at migrations 001-023 and preserves the exact 54-table source contract; repository migration 024 is separately classified as post-cutover dormant with current production disposition unknown.
The production runtime ACL refuses any table, sequence or function inventory outside exact 001-023 before granting roles; migration 024 explicitly revokes PUBLIC execution from both E3 functions.

independentReviews.evidence: 78 focused tests plus 7 selected callback, descriptor-failure and strict-ID regressions passed on the final bytes.
Exact binding, 19 selected lifecycle/FD probes, compilation and diff checks passed on the final bytes.
All nine hashes, current read-only registry chain, PostgreSQL 17.11 floor, Docker stdin/digest semantics and archive ownership caveats were independently checked.

operationalBlockers: No production source, dump or restore adapter exists; real argv execution and receipts have not been observed.
The obsidian_b64_snapshot_reader principal is not provisioned or independently attested in production.
Authentication against a production registry, trusted time, fresh revocation and durable atomic replay is not implemented.
No fresh exact-plan owner authorization or separate independent-reviewer acceptance exists; the prior conversational authorization is unconsumed and cannot cover changed bytes.
The source network namespace is shared and egress isolation is not proved.
The core deadline is fail-closed after callbacks return but remains cooperative; a real adapter must enforce process kill and bounded cleanup externally.
External copies and physical erasure are outside the verified cleanup scope.
No authorization-time registry/CVE revalidation has occurred and the frozen mutable-tag observation cannot prove future security.
